To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hydrodynamic shear stress promotes the conversion of circulating tumor cells into specific stem cell-like cells that are capable of initiating tumor formation in the lung and bone marrow.
fluid shear stress experienced during circulation of human tumor cells can lead specific acquisition of stem cell potential that promotes E-MET and metastasis.

fluid shear stress experienced during circulation of human breast cancer cells leads to acquisition of mesenchyme stem cell (MSC) like potential that promotes epithelial-mesonchymal transition, and metastatic spread to distant organs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of hydrodynamic shear in the conversion of epithelial tumor cells to mesenchymal CSLCs/TIC, which is important in the development and progression of breast cancer.
the role of hydrodynamic shear force in the metastatic cascade and the acquisition of TIC potential in CTCs.
the effects of hydrodynamic shear force in the tumor microcirculation and its role in promoting tumor progression, metastasis, and cancer stem cell-like properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

shear stress promotes conversion of epithelial cancer cells into CSLCs/TIC-like cells via a mechanism that is similar to that of MSCs and that is dependent on suppression of ERK/GSK3β activities and on ROS/NO generation.
the fluid microenvironment is an important regulator that drives cancer metastasis and may be a novel target for the development of therapeutic strategies to prevent or treat metastatic disease.

fluid shear stress experienced during the systemic circulation of tumor cells can lead specifically to the acquisition of MSC-like potential and promote EMT, meso-epithelial reversion, and metastasis of human breast cancer to distant organs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
+SS is the driving force that converts epithelial tumor cells in the primary tumor into distinct CSLCs/TIC in the circulation.
+SS is an essential factor that can promote EMT, meso-epi transition, and metastatic potential of CTCs.

hydrodynamic shear stress experienced during the circulation of human breast cancer cells can lead to the specific acquisition of meso- or stem-like potential that promotes EEMT, MET, and metastasis of breast cancer to distant organs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
+SS is an important factor that promotes the acquisition of CSLC/TIC potential by CTCs during metastasis.
+SS can induce EMT-like transition and acquisition of TIC potential in circulating epithelial cells, which may be important for metastasis and relapse of human breast cancers.
biomechanical shear stress in the blood circulation can lead to specific conversion of CTC into TICs, which can then promote metastatic colonization in distant tissues.
